{{short description|Award in mathematics}}
The '''Blackwell–Tapia Prize''' is a [[mathematics]] award that recognizes active mathematical scientists who have (1) contributed and continue to contribute significantly to research in their fields of expertise, and (2) served as role models for mathematical scientists and students from underrepresented minority groups or contributed in other significant ways to addressing the problem of the underrepresentation of minorities in mathematics <ref name = "MSI Diversity Initiative">{{cite web |url=https://mathinstitutes.org/diversity/blackwell-tapia-conference |title=Blackwell-Tapia Conference |website=[[NIMBioS]] |access-date=20 October 2023}}</ref> It is presented every other year at the Blackwell-Tapia Conference,<ref name=mathinstitutes>{{cite web |url=https://mathinstitutes.org/diversity/blackwell-tapia-conference/ |title=Blackwell-Tapia Conference and Award Ceremony |access-date=16 January 2018 |website=[[National Science Foundation]]}}</ref> which promotes mathematical excellence by minority researchers and is sponsored by the [[National Science Foundation]]. The prize is named for [[David Blackwell]] and [[Richard Tapia]]. <ref>{{cite journal |last1=Buckmire |first1=R |date=2019 |title=Recognizing Black and Latinx Mathematical Excellence: The Blackwell–Tapia Prize |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201902/rnoti-p218.pdf |journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |volume=66 |issue=2 |pages=218-220 |doi=10.1090/noti1798  |doi-access=free|access-date=20 October 2023}}</ref>
